summary: MariaDB is configured on node1 and verified across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the inventory database and InnoDB items table.
Created inventory_app@localhost with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges on inventory.*.
Generated a 48-character credential on node1 and stored it in /etc/inventory-db.env as a root-owned regular file with mode 0600.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified service, schema, account, credential authentication, and transactional table access after recovery.

evidence.summary: Installation completed; MariaDB is enabled, active, listening, and responds to an administrative ping after reboot.
Created inventory.items; metadata confirms an InnoDB table using utf8mb4_unicode_ci, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Local application account with working generated credential
evidence.summary: inventory_app exists only at localhost with a nonempty generated credential and only DELETE, INSERT, SELECT, and UPDATE privileges on inventory.*. Authentication and a rolled-back table transaction succeeded after reboot.
The credential file is a regular file owned by root:root with mode 0600; its keys were inspected with values redacted.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 45c22b1f-31bf-419b-a1a4-331c4aa1a40a; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node1 returned with changed boot ID bc5b85d1-d6e2-4a74-b5a9-e3b26b48a289; complete service, data, account, file-permission, and application-access recovery was verified.
